facts.name: Eligibility requirements
facts.must_capture: Every eligibility condition: nationality, local-candidate status, marital or dependants clauses if any, disqualifications, and any post-specific condition.

value.provisional_at_all_stages: Admission at every stage is purely provisional and subject to satisfying the prescribed conditions; issue of a hall ticket does not mean candidature has been cleared. Verification against original documents happens only after a candidate has finally qualified, or at an appropriate time chosen by the board.
value.gender: Codes 11, 12, 16, 17 — men and women; codes 13, 14, 18 — men only; code 19 — women only.
value.post_specific: Post Code 17 additionally requires a valid Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) driving licence held as on the date of notification, with the licence information to be produced at certificate verification.
value.medical_eyesight: Distant vision 6/6 in each eye and near vision 0/5 (Snellen) in each eye; each eye must have a full field of vision; colour blindness, squint or any morbid condition of the eye or lids of either eye is a disqualification.
value.general_health: The candidate must possess sound health and be free from any bodily defect or infirmity that would render them unfit.
value.disqualifying_conditions: Physically handicapped; knock-knees, pigeon chest, flat foot, varicose veins, hammer toes, fractured limbs, decayed teeth, stammering, hard of hearing, and abnormal psychological behaviour.
value.medical_examination_route: Provisionally selected candidates are referred to the District Headquarter Hospital; expert opinion goes to Osmania or Gandhi Hospitals, and eye cases to Sarojini Devi Eye Hospital, whose opinion is final. A candidate may be referred or examined only once on such a recommendation.
value.local_candidate_status: Local-candidate status under the Presidential Order 2018 is not a condition for applying, but it governs eligibility for every reservation and for age relaxation. Candidates who are not local to Telangana State are not entitled to any kind of reservation.
value.honesty_conditions: Furnishing false, tampered or fabricated particulars, or suppressing material information, attracts punitive action under law; impersonation attracts criminal prosecution besides disqualification. An incomplete or incorrect application form is summarily rejected and later corrections are not entertained.
value.attendance: Appearance in all tests and written examinations is compulsory; absence in any of them automatically renders a candidate disqualified.

facts.name: Educational qualifications
facts.must_capture: The required qualification per post code, the cut-off date by which it must be held, and how equivalence is treated.

value.requirement: A Degree awarded by any university in India established or incorporated by or under a Central Act or a Provincial Act of a State, or of any institution recognised by the University Grants Commission, or any other equivalent qualification.
value.cut_off_date: The qualification must be held as on the date of notification, i.e. 29 July 2026.
value.proof_required: A Degree, Provisional Certificate, or Consolidated Marks Memo covering the whole duration of study, issued by the university on or before 29 July 2026, must be produced at certificate verification. Failure to produce it on the designated day means the candidate is deemed not to possess the qualification and is not carried forward. Certificates produced after the last date of certificate verification are not considered.
value.distance_education: Degrees obtained through Open Universities or the distance-education mode require recognition by the UGC, AICTE or Distance Education Council as applicable; unrecognised degrees are not accepted, and the onus of proving recognition rests on the candidate.
value.higher_qualification: A candidate holding a higher qualification than the prescribed one is considered on par with a candidate holding the prescribed one.
value.per_post_code: The notification states this single degree requirement under Para 15-C without differentiating by post code. The only post-specific addition anywhere in Para 15 is Para 15-D, the LMV driving licence for Post Code 17. Recorded as read: one common degree requirement plus one post-specific technical requirement.
value.language_qualification_standard: Not an entry qualification, but relevant: the qualifying English paper and the qualifying Telugu or Urdu paper in the Final Written Examination are of Matriculation or equivalent standard.

facts.name: Age requirements
facts.must_capture: Minimum and maximum age, the reference date on which age is computed, and every relaxation with the category it applies to.

value.reference_date: 1 July 2026. Age is computed as on that date, not as on the notification date.
value.minimum_age: Must have attained 21 years as on 1 July 2026.
value.base_maximum_age: Must not have attained 25 years as on 1 July 2026.
value.general_raise_in_notification: The notification records that GO Ms No. 87, General Administration (Services-A) Department, dated 18-05-2026 raised the upper age limit for direct recruitment to uniformed services in the Police, Fire Services, Prisons and Special Protection Force Departments by 5 years, and states that this relaxation is in addition to the upper age limit above.
value.further_raise_by_supplementary: The supplementary notification of 15 August 2026 records that GO Ms No. 122, General Administration (Services-A) Department, dated 14-08-2026 raised the upper age limit by a further 2 years in addition to the 5 years of GO Ms No. 87, and names Para No. 15-B (i) of this notification as the paragraph affected.

category_relaxations.telangana_state_government_employees: Length of regular service subject to a maximum of 5 years. Employees of TS TRANSCO, DISCOMs, TS GENCO, the State Road Transport Corporation, other Telangana State corporations, municipalities, local bodies and public sector undertakings are expressly not entitled to this relaxation.
category_relaxations.ex_servicemen: 3 years in addition to the length of service rendered in the Armed Forces (Army, Navy, Air Force or Territorial Army).

facts.name: Reservation and category rules
facts.must_capture: Reservation percentages and rules as the notification states them, including horizontal reservations and the certificate each requires.

value.governing_rule: Special Representation (Reservation) under Rule 22 of the Telangana State and Subordinate Service Rules, 1996 applies to all the posts, covering BC-A, BC-B, BC-C, BC-D, BC-E, SC, ST, Ex-Servicemen, Meritorious Sports Person and Economically Weaker Section. Rule 22-A of the same rules applies only to Post Code Nos. 11, 16 and 17.
value.no_percentages_printed_for_communal_cate: The notification does not print percentage figures for SC, ST or the BC groups. It incorporates Rule 22 by reference. Any specific communal percentage therefore has no basis in either document and is deliberately absent here.

D) Department dated 19.03.2021 read with GO Ms No. 244 dated 24-08-2021, issued by a District Magistrate, Additional District Magistrate, Collector, Sub-divisional Magistrate, Mandal Revenue Officer, a revenue officer not below the rank of Tahsildar, or the Sub-Divisional Officer of the area of residence.

value.locality_precondition: BC, SC and ST candidates who are not local to Telangana State as per the Presidential Order 2018 are not entitled to any kind of reservation. EWS and Meritorious Sports Person reservation likewise require local-candidate status, and all Special Category reservations are for Telangana local candidates only.
value.bc_e_caveat: Age relaxation and reservation for BC-E are subject to pending litigation including final orders in Civil Appeal No(s). 2628-2637 of 2010 in SLP No. 7388-97 of 2010 dated 25-03-2010 and to government orders.
value.meritorious_sports_person_categories: Category 1 is a sportsperson who won medals or represented India in an international or multinational competition in a game recognised in Annexure I of GO Ms No. 74, YATC (Sports) Department dated 9-8-2012. Category 2 is a sportsperson who won medals or represented a State of India in a national competition in such a game. Category 1 is exhausted before Category 2 is considered; within a category, final-selection marks decide inter-se merit; unfilled MSP vacancies go to Open Competition in the same recruitment.
value.women_reservation: 33⅓% of the vacancies in each category including EWS are reserved for women for Post Code Nos. 11, 16 and 17, and 10% of the vacancies in each category including EWS are reserved for women for Post Code No. 12. It is a horizontal reservation on the principle of sufficiency, adjusted proportionately within the woman candidate's own communal category. Unfilled women's vacancies are not carried forward and are filled by men of the same communal category. Post Code Nos. 13, 14 and 18 are men-only and Post Code No. 19 is women-only, so no women's quota is stated for them.
value.special_categories_horizontal: Police Executive (PE), Police Ministerial (PM), Members of Telangana Special Protection Force (MoSPF), National Cadet Corps (NCC), Children of Police Personnel (CPP), Children of Deceased and Incapacitated Police Personnel (CDI), Children of Telangana Special Protection Force (CSPF), Children of Prisons Department Personnel (CJP) and Children of members of Fire Services (CFSP) are adjusted horizontally within the candidate's own communal category, and the percentage is computed for each category on the vacancies notified.
value.pe_pm_service_condition: A Police Executive or Police Ministerial claimant must have completed three years of service as on the date of the notification.
value.local_reservation: Local reservation is governed by Para (7) of the Telangana Public Employment (Presidential Order), 2018, and the notification's Para 19 sets out how local and non-local candidates are treated in the zone-wise allocation.

facts.name: Preliminary Written Test structure
facts.must_capture: Whether the PWT is one paper or several, objective or otherwise, its mode, and whether it is qualifying or counts towards the final merit.

value.mode: Objective, answered on an OMR answer sheet using a blue or black ball-point pen only. The hall ticket is issued online.
value.role_in_selection: Screening. The PWT is the gate to the PMT / PET: candidates who qualify in it are called for the PMT / PET by an intimation letter downloaded from www.tgprb.in. Para 16-E, which sets out final selection, computes merit from the Final Written Examination papers (and, for some post codes, PET run marks), and does not include PWT marks. Recorded as read from Para 16-A, Para 16-E and the intimation-letter paragraph; the notification does not use the word 'screening' itself.
value.language: Questions are set in English-Telugu and English-Urdu. Where scientific, technological or management terminology is involved, transliteration is used at the expert's discretion. If a Telugu or Urdu translation or transliteration is ambiguous or misspelt, the English version is final and correct.
value.deleted_question_treatment: Where any question is deleted in the final answer key, each candidate is compensated with reference to the deleted questions in proportion to the percentage of marks obtained in the remaining undeleted questions.

facts.name: Minimum qualifying requirements
facts.must_capture: Qualifying marks or percentages per stage and per category, and any separate sectional minimum.

preliminary_written_test.basis: Of the paper as a whole. The PWT is one paper of 200 marks, so the thresholds are 60, 50 and 40 marks respectively — arithmetic recorded in `derived`, not printed.

final_written_examination.basis: In each paper, not on the aggregate. Failing the minimum in any one paper ends the candidature.

value.special_categories: Candidates of the special categories referred to in Para 21 take the minimum qualifying marks of their own social category.
value.sectional_minimum_within_a_paper: None stated. The PWT covers two subjects in one paper and no per-subject minimum is prescribed; the FWE minimum is per paper, which is the finest granularity the document gives.
value.papers_I_and_II_are_qualifying_only: Papers I and II are qualifying in nature and their marks are not taken into account for final selection, but failing the minimum in them ends the candidature irrespective of performance in Papers III and IV.
value.oc_ews_eligibility_rule: A candidate who secures 40% and above in each of Paper III and Paper IV is eligible to be considered for selection to posts under OC / EWS irrespective of their social category. This is an upward route into the open category, not an additional hurdle.
value.physical_stages: The PMT and PET standards are pass or fail thresholds rather than percentages; they are recorded in OFF-F18 and OFF-F19. For Post Code Nos. 12, 13, 14 and 16 the run additionally carries marks, so for those posts it is both a qualifying threshold and a scored event.
value.no_right_from_minimum: Mere securing of minimum qualifying marks does not vest any right in a candidate to be considered for selection.
value.compulsory_appearance: Appearance in all the tests and written examinations is compulsory; absence in any of them automatically renders a candidate disqualified.

run.conduct: Where RFID-based readings are taken, competitors perform totally independently of each other and start time, finish time and duration are recorded individually. Where required, only the curved-start method is adopted, so competitors may change lanes immediately after the start.

The normalised marks are what is used in drawing the final merit list, and are rounded up to the third decimal place and taken as they are. The formula's terms are defined on pages 21 and 22 as SD (standard deviation), Avg (mean), subscript T (all qualified candidates), subscript S (all qualified candidates of the candidate's gender group), subscript TT (the top 0.1% or top 10, whichever is higher, among all qualified candidates) and subscript ST (the same top group within the candidate's gender group).

facts.name: Final Written Examination structure
facts.must_capture: Number of papers, their mode, whether descriptive or objective, and how the FWE contributes to final merit.

value.who_appears: Candidates who qualify in the Physical Efficiency Test. Hall tickets are issued to them with venue, date and time, and the hall ticket must be brought to the examination.

paper_I.subject: English

how_fwe_contributes_to_merit.post_codes_11_17_18_19: Final selection strictly on relative merit from the aggregate score of Paper III and Paper IV. The PET run is qualifying only for these posts, so the written aggregate is the whole of merit.
how_fwe_contributes_to_merit.post_codes_12_and_16: Final selection on relative merit from the score of the Final Written Examination (Papers III and IV) together with the Physical Efficiency Test (1600 / 800 metres run), with men's and women's PET marks normalised by the TSLPRB formula; the normalised marks are the basis of the final common merit list.
how_fwe_contributes_to_merit.post_codes_13_and_14: Final selection on relative merit from the aggregate score of the Final Written Examination (Papers III and IV) together with the Physical Efficiency Test (1600 metres run). No normalisation clause appears for these two, which are men-only posts.
how_fwe_contributes_to_merit.papers_I_and_II: Excluded from merit in every case; they are qualifying only, and their marks are expressly not taken into account for final selection.

value.answer_medium: Part A of Papers I and II and the whole of Papers III and IV are answered on an OMR answer sheet using a blue or black ball-point pen only. Part B of Papers I and II is descriptive.
value.language_of_papers_III_and_IV: Set in English-Telugu and English-Urdu, with transliteration at the expert's discretion for scientific, technological or management terminology. If a Telugu or Urdu translation or transliteration is ambiguous or misspelt, the English version is final and correct.
value.deleted_question_treatment: While evaluating objective-type papers, marks for deleted questions are awarded proportionately and considered up to three decimal places to determine merit; each candidate is compensated in proportion to the percentage of marks obtained in the remaining undeleted questions.
value.no_postponement: Candidates must be fit in all aspects at all stages including the PMT and PET; no postponement or reconsideration of any stage is allowed under any circumstances, and the tests must be undergone on the designated day in the prescribed sequential order.
value.tie_break: Where two or more candidates in a particular category obtain equal marks, preference is given to the candidate who was born earlier.

value.differences_from_the_pwt_syllabus: Four differences are recorded rather than reconciled. First, Paper IV has seven items where the PWT General Studies has six: the personality-test item is inserted at position six and Telangana Movement moves from six to seven. Second, item 3 reads 'History of India (including Indian National Movement) – emphasis will be on broad and general understanding' in Annexure II but 'History of India – emphasis will be on broad general understanding ... Indian National Movement' in Annexure III, so the Indian National Movement is parenthetical in one and a trailing clause in the other, and the word 'and' is present in one phrase and absent in the other. Third, the Arithmetic and Test of Reasoning paragraphs read 'It will include' in Annexure II and 'It shall include' in Annexure III, and Annexure III has 'include question on analogies' where Annexure II has 'questions on analogies'. Fourth, question counts double from 100 to 200 per subject. Because the wording differs, the two annexures are stored as two separate syllabus trees and neither is used to fill a gap in the other.
value.textbook_position: As in Annexure II: the Board prescribes no particular textbook or publication and is not bound by material appearing in any book or publication, and the Subject Expert Committee's decision on a disputed question or answer is final.

facts.name: Selection sequence
facts.must_capture: The ordered stages from application to final selection, which stages are eliminating, which contribute marks, and the ratio used to shortlist at each stage.

stages_in_order.name: Online registration and application with fee payment
stages_in_order.who: All applicants, via www.tgprb.in with the mobile number as user ID
stages_in_order.eliminating: Yes — an ineligible application can be rejected at any time, and fee once paid is not refunded

stages_in_order.name: Preliminary Written Test
stages_in_order.eliminating: Yes — 30% OC including EWS, 25% BC, 20% SC / ST / Ex-Servicemen
stages_in_order.note: One paper, three hours, 200 questions, 200 marks. Qualifiers download an intimation letter for the PMT / PET.

stages_in_order.name: Physical Efficiency Test — run
stages_in_order.who: Candidates who qualify in the Preliminary Written Test
stages_in_order.eliminating: Yes — 1600 m in 7 min 15 sec for men, 9 min 30 sec for Ex-Servicemen, 800 m in 5 min 20 sec for women
stages_in_order.contributes_marks: Only for Post Code Nos. 12, 13, 14 and 16, per the Annexure I gradation table; qualifying only for Post Code Nos. 11, 17, 18 and 19

stages_in_order.name: Physical Measurements — height
stages_in_order.who: Candidates who qualify in the run event
stages_in_order.eliminating: Yes — 167.6 cm men and 152.5 cm women generally, 160 cm and 150 cm for ST and Aboriginal Tribes candidates of the nine named agency districts

stages_in_order.name: Physical Efficiency Test — long jump and shot-put
stages_in_order.who: Candidates declared qualified in the physical measurements

stages_in_order.name: Final Written Examination
stages_in_order.who: Candidates who qualify in the Physical Efficiency Test
stages_in_order.eliminating: Yes — 40% OC including EWS, 35% BC, 30% SC / ST / Ex-Servicemen in each paper
stages_in_order.contributes_marks: Papers III and IV only; Papers I and II are qualifying in nature and their marks are not counted

stages_in_order.name: Certificates Verification
stages_in_order.who: Candidates who are qualified in the Final Written Examination
stages_in_order.eliminating: Yes — failure to produce originals on the day of verification, or a mismatch with the online application, means the candidature is rejected or disqualified without further correspondence

stages_in_order.name: Final selection on relative merit
stages_in_order.note: 95% of the vacancies in the respective Zones or Contiguous Zones are filled from local candidates of those zones for Post Code Nos. 11, 12, 14, 17, 18 and 19; the 2018 Order does not apply to Post Code Nos. 13 and 16, where local status is instead a precondition for any vertical or horizontal reservation. Equal marks are broken in favour of the candidate born earlier.

stages_in_order.name: Antecedents verification and medical examination
stages_in_order.eliminating: Yes — selection is provisional and subject to verification of original certificates, antecedents, medical fitness and the outcome of any pending disciplinary proceedings
stages_in_order.note: Provisionally selected candidates are referred to the District Headquarters Hospital; expert opinion goes to Osmania or Gandhi Hospital, and eye cases to Sarojini Devi Eye Hospital whose opinion is final. A candidate can be referred or examined only once.

stages_in_order.name: Induction training and appointment
stages_in_order.eliminating: Not a selection stage, but a candidate who cannot join the original induction batch for reasons attributable to them must re-pass the Physical Efficiency Test as prescribed on the date of that later test before being considered
stages_in_order.note: Stipend is payable during institutional training for Post Code Nos. 11 to 14 and 16; appointment to the regular post follows successful completion.

facts.name: Official instructions affecting preparation
facts.must_capture: Instructions that change how a candidate should prepare: permitted languages and any language-of-question rule, calculator or device rules, syllabus annexures, translation-discrepancy clauses, tie-breaking rules, and any stated bar on material outside the syllabus.

value.syllabus_location: Annexure II is the Preliminary Written Test syllabus; Annexure III is the Final Written Examination syllabus. There is no third syllabus annexure and no separate detailed syllabus document referenced.
value.language_of_question_papers: The PWT paper and FWE Papers III and IV are set in English-Telugu and English-Urdu. For terminology of science, technology or management, transliteration is employed at the expert's discretion.
value.translation_discrepancy_clause: In case of any ambiguity or spelling mistake in translation or transliteration in any question in the Telugu or Urdu language, the English version is considered final and the correct version. This is stated separately for the PWT and for Papers III and IV, in near-identical wording.
value.second_language_choice: In Paper II a candidate chooses Telugu or Urdu, must indicate the choice when asked, and cannot change it subsequently.
value.answer_medium_rules: Objective answers go on an OMR answer sheet using a blue or black ball-point pen only — stated for the PWT, for Part A of Papers I and II, and for Papers III and IV.
value.textbook_and_dispute_position: The Board does not prescribe any particular textbook or publication and is not bound by material appearing in any book or publication. Where there is a dispute about any question or answer, the decision of the Subject Expert Committee is final. Both statements appear at the foot of Annexure II and again at the foot of Annexure III.
value.no_bar_on_material_outside_the_syllabus: The notification states no bar on material outside the annexures. What it states instead is that the Board is not bound by any book or publication, and both Arithmetic and Test of Reasoning scopes end with 'etc'. The practical implication recorded here is that the printed lists are illustrative, not exhaustive — an inference about scope, not a stated rule, and marked as such.
value.deleted_question_compensation: PWT: each candidate is compensated for deleted questions in proportion to the percentage of marks obtained in the remaining undeleted questions. FWE objective papers: the same, with marks considered up to three decimal places to determine merit.
value.tie_breaking_rule: Where two or more candidates in a particular category obtain equal marks, preference is given to the candidate born earlier. There is no second tie-break criterion.
value.rounding_rules_that_affect_outcomes: PET digital readings are rounded mathematically to 2 decimal places for qualification and gradation; normalised run marks for Post Code Nos. 12 and 16 are rounded up to the third decimal place; deleted-question compensation in the FWE is carried to three decimal places.
value.route_into_the_open_category: A candidate who secures 40% and above in each of Paper III and Paper IV is eligible to be considered for OC / EWS posts irrespective of social category.
value.compulsory_appearance_and_no_postponemen: Appearance in all tests and written examinations is compulsory and absence disqualifies automatically; no postponement or reconsideration of any stage is allowed, and candidates must be fit in all aspects at all stages.
value.single_pmt_pet_across_notifications: For applications to more than one TSLPRB notification issued within three months, the PMT and PET are conducted once and the same readings and scores apply to all posts applied for. The four sibling notifications named in the fee paragraph are Rc. 225 (SCT SI Civil or equivalent), Rc. 279 (SCT ASI FPB), Rc. 189 (SCT PC Civil or equivalent) and Rc. 234 (SCT PC Mechanic and SCT PC Driver). A rebate of Rs.50 per additional post applies to Telangana-local SC and ST candidates and Rs.100 to all others.
value.authoritative_channel: The TSLPRB website is final, legitimate and definitive for correspondence and communication with candidates; no individual correspondence by any other means is entertained. Candidates are advised to visit the website regularly and not to rely on rumours or false propaganda on media or social media platforms. TSLPRB reserves the right to modify and reschedule examinations, and its decisions are final.
value.calculator_and_device_rules_status: NOT_ADDRESSED. A word-boundary search of both extraction artefacts finds zero occurrences of 'calculator', 'calculators', 'watch', 'mobile', 'prohibited', 'banned' and 'malpractice'. The single occurrence of 'electronic' and of 'devices' is the note that candidature is processed through computer or electronic devices, which concerns application processing, not the examination hall. No permitted or prohibited item list appears in either document.
value.examination_dates: Not stated. Neither document contains a PWT, PET or FWE date, and the application window itself is deferred to a future press release, so no examination calendar can be built from these two documents. See OFF-F03.

unresolved.question: What items may a candidate carry into the examination hall, and is any calculating or electronic device permitted?
unresolved.observation: Zero word-boundary occurrences of 'calculator', 'calculators', 'watch', 'mobile', 'prohibited', 'banned' or 'malpractice' in either extraction artefact. The only instruction about what a candidate brings is the hall ticket or intimation letter, and the only instruction about writing implements is that a blue or black ball-point pen must be used on the OMR sheet.
unresolved.why_it_matters: Arithmetic preparation strategy depends on it: 200 arithmetic questions in three hours implies mental and pen-and-paper computation, and a candidate who assumed otherwise would train the wrong skill. The safe working assumption is no calculating aid, but that is an inference and is not recorded as an official rule.
